part.text:
This is the classic PaaS IO counter exercise. The interfaces are already defined in `interface.go`, so I just need to implement the counters in `paasio.go`. Key requirements from the tests:

- Counts must be updated atomically (bytes + ops together under one lock), because `testReadCountConsistency`/`testWriteCountConsistency` check that `nops == n/numBytes` at any snapshot.
- `nops` counts every call to `Read()`/`Write()`, while `n` counts only bytes successfully returned.
One cleanup — construct the embedded counters directly instead of via type assertion:

All tests pass, including with the race detector (`go test -race -count=1 ./...` → `ok paasio`).

I implemented the solution entirely in `paasio.go` (the interfaces were already defined in `interface.go`, and I didn't touch `paasio_test.go`):

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`; `Read` delegates to the wrapped reader, then atomically adds the returned byte count and increments the call count under a mutex. `ReadCount` returns both under the same lock.
- **`writeCounter`** — the same pattern for `io.Writer` / `WriteCount`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — embeds a `*readCounter` and a `*writeCounter` (each with its own lock), so it satisfies `ReadWriteCounter` without a single shared lock serializing reads and writes.

The design matches the interface contract: bytes and operation counts are updated together under one lock per direction, so a `ReadCount`/`WriteCount` snapshot can never observe a torn state — which is exactly what the `testReadCountConsistency` / `testWriteCountConsistency` tests check under 4000 concurrent goroutines.
